title: CTS, VTS, Gerrit, and an AOSP Contribution

scout.purpose: Master cts, vts, gerrit, and an aosp contribution through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Specialist Android work must remain compatible, secure, measurable, accessible, distributable, and operable outside a demonstration.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend cts, vts, gerrit, and an aosp contribution.

blocks.text: Platform confidence layers include focused unit or integration tests, host tests, device tests, CTS for Android application and API compatibility, and VTS for vendor, HAL, kernel, and Treble contracts. Run the narrowest relevant suite during development and the required compatibility scope before submission. A passing local test does not replace build, boot, security, API, and presubmit evidence. Flakes require reproduction and ownership rather than repeated reruns until green.

blocks.text: AOSP contributions require the appropriate contributor agreement, project branch created with repo start, a focused commit with Change-Id, tests, and a clear problem, cause, solution, and evidence. repo upload sends changes to Gerrit. OWNERS review, automated checks, and patchsets refine the same logical change; amend rather than creating unrelated replacement commits. Multi-project work needs coordinated changes and topics. Upstream external projects should receive fixes upstream when appropriate.

blocks.code: repo start droidquest-fix .; git add -A; git commit; repo upload --current-branch
blocks.caption: A focused fragment whose complete contract includes exact versions, ownership, adverse paths, compatibility, and release evidence.

blocks.text: Prepare a reproducible bug, minimal patch, negative and positive tests, module build, boot or device evidence, API and compatibility impact, and no unrelated formatting. Respond to review with evidence, rebase carefully, rerun affected tests, and preserve authorship. Study merged precedent and ownership before implementation. A change may be correct but unsuitable for public API, release branch, or architecture; accept redesign. Document rollback and flag strategy for risky platform work.

Expert engineering makes assumptions, authority, compatibility, security, privacy, accessibility, performance, distribution, and recovery reviewable. Begin with a concrete user or platform outcome, identify trust and lifecycle boundaries, and retain exact source, dependency, toolchain, configuration, model or platform version, and artifact identity. Test realistic success plus denial, offline, process death, cancellation, corruption, version skew, resource pressure, and dependency failure. Measure representative distributions rather than best runs. Document unsupported cases, residual risk, owners, release gates, incident response, deprecation, and rollback or roll-forward. A specialised solution is production-ready only when another team can integrate, verify, operate, upgrade, disable, and remove it safely.

trap_check.mistake: Uploading a new commit without the original Change-Id creates a separate Gerrit change instead of a new patchset for the review.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

challenge_intro.task: Prepare a real or simulated AOSP change with reproduction, focused patch, tests, build and boot evidence, OWNERS selection, Gerrit patchsets, and review responses.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The work includes a minimal coherent implementation, exact evidence, support and threat boundaries, adverse testing, release operation, and recovery.

recall.prompt: What keeps amended commits grouped as patchsets of one Gerrit review?
recall.answer: The stable Change-Id footer in the commit message.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.

objectives: Explain and defend the complete contract behind CTS, VTS, Gerrit, and an AOSP Contribution.
